title: Lead RRP lead hazard standards and abatement basics practice questions
description: Free practice questions on EPA lead hazard standards and abatement basics (40 CFR 745 Subparts D and L), each answer quoted and linked to its section.

questions.question: What does 745.61(c) say Subpart D requires of the owner of a property subject to the lead-based paint hazard standards?

options.A: The owner must have a risk assessment done before selling or renting the property
options.B: The owner must abate any identified hazard within a period the subpart sets
options.C: Nothing in the subpart requires the owner to evaluate the property for hazards or to act to control any that are identified
options.D: The owner must have every friction surface tested once a year

questions.explanation: 745.61(c): "Nothing in this subpart requires the owner of property(ies) subject to these standards to evaluate the property(ies) for the presence of lead-based paint hazards or take any action to control these conditions if one or more of them is identified."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.61, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Nothing in this subpart requires the owner of property(ies) subject to these standards to evaluate the property(ies) for the presence of lead-based paint hazards or take any action to control these conditions if one or more of them is identified.

questions.question: Under 745.61(d), what are the levels in 745.227(e)(8)(viii) referred to as on or after January 13, 2025?

options.A: Action levels
options.B: Hazard levels
options.C: Reportable levels
options.D: Screening levels

questions.explanation: 745.61(d): "On or after January 13, 2025, the levels identified in § 745.227(e)(8)(viii) are referred to as action levels." Before that date they "were referred to as clearance levels."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.61, Scope and applicability (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: On or after January 13, 2025, the levels identified in § 745.227(e)(8)(viii) are referred to as action levels.

questions.question: Under 745.65(a)(1), when is lead-based paint on a friction surface that is subject to abrasion a paint-lead hazard?

options.A: Whenever the friction surface is also a chewable surface
options.B: Only when the friction surface is on the exterior of the building
options.C: Whenever any lead-based paint is on the friction surface, whatever the dust levels nearby
options.D: When lead dust levels on the nearest horizontal surface underneath it are equal to or greater than the dust-lead hazard levels in 745.65(b)

questions.explanation: 745.65(a)(1) covers lead-based paint on a friction surface "where the lead dust levels on the nearest horizontal surface underneath the friction surface (e.g., the window sill, or floor) are equal to or greater than the dust-lead hazard levels identified in paragraph (b) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.65, Lead-based paint hazards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: where the lead dust levels on the nearest horizontal surface underneath the friction surface (e.g., the window sill, or floor) are equal to or greater than the dust-lead hazard levels identified in paragraph (b) of this section.

questions.question: Under 745.65(a)(3), what makes a chewable lead-based painted surface a paint-lead hazard?

options.A: A child under 6 years of age lives in the dwelling
options.B: Evidence of teeth marks on the surface
options.C: A child's blood lead level has been found elevated
options.D: The surface is a window sill

questions.explanation: 745.65(a)(3): "Any chewable lead-based painted surface on which there is evidence of teeth marks."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.65, Lead-based paint hazards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: Any chewable lead-based painted surface on which there is evidence of teeth marks.

questions.question: Besides surfaces tested and found at or above the lead-based paint threshold, on which other surfaces does 745.227(h)(1)(ii) say lead-based paint is present?

options.A: Every painted surface in the building once any one surface tests positive
options.B: Any surface like a surface tested in the same room equivalent that has a similar painting history and that is found to be lead-based paint
options.C: Any painted surface in a building constructed prior to 1978
options.D: Any surface the owner reports was painted before the building was sold

questions.explanation: 745.227(h)(1)(ii): lead-based paint is present "On any surface like a surface tested in the same room equivalent that has a similar painting history and that is found to be lead-based paint."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: On any surface like a surface tested in the same room equivalent that has a similar painting history and that is found to be lead-based paint.

questions.question: On or after January 12, 2026, what does 745.65(b) define as a dust-lead hazard in a residential dwelling or child-occupied facility?

options.A: Surface dust with 25 µg/ft2 or more of lead on floors or 200 µg/ft2 or more on interior window sills
options.B: Any visible dust on floors or interior window sills, whether or not it is sampled
options.C: Surface dust with any reportable level of lead on window troughs only
options.D: Surface dust with any reportable level of lead for floors or for interior window sills, based on wipe samples analyzed by an NLLAP-recognized laboratory

questions.explanation: 745.65(b): "On or after January 12, 2026, a dust-lead hazard is surface dust in a residential dwelling or child-occupied facility that contains a mass-per-area concentration of any reportable level of lead for floors or for interior window sills based on wipe samples analyzed by an NLLAP-recognized laboratory."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.65, Lead-based paint hazards (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: On or after January 12, 2026, a dust-lead hazard is surface dust in a residential dwelling or child-occupied facility that contains a mass-per-area concentration of any reportable level of lead for floors or for interior window sills based on wipe samples analyzed by an NLLAP-recognized laboratory.

questions.question: What action level does 745.227(e)(8)(viii) set for lead in dust on window troughs on or after January 12, 2026?

options.A: 100 µg/ft2
options.B: 50 µg/ft2
options.C: 200 µg/ft2
options.D: 250 µg/ft2

questions.explanation: 745.227(e)(8)(viii): "On or after January 12, 2026, the action levels for lead in dust are 5 µg/ft2 for floors, 40 µg/ft2 for interior window sills, and 100 µg/ft2 for window troughs."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: On or after January 12, 2026, the action levels for lead in dust are 5 µg/ft2 for floors, 40 µg/ft2 for interior window sills, and 100 µg/ft2 for window troughs.

questions.question: Under the 745.223 definition of action levels, what must be achieved to complete abatement when dust sampling is required?

options.A: Values at or above the action levels
options.B: Values below the soil-lead hazard levels
options.C: Values below the action levels
options.D: No visible dust; sample results are not compared with any level

questions.explanation: 745.223: action levels "are the values that indicate the amount of lead in dust on a surface following completion of an abatement activity. To complete abatement when dust sampling is required, values below these levels must be achieved."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.223, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: To complete abatement when dust sampling is required, values below these levels must be achieved.

questions.question: When soil is removed during a soil abatement, what does 745.227(e)(7)(i)(B) say about the soil that is removed?

options.A: It may be reused as top soil at another residential property if mixed with clean soil
options.B: It may be used as top soil at another residential property if it is tested first
options.C: It may be used as top soil at a child-occupied facility if covered with mulch
options.D: It shall not be used as top soil at another residential property or child-occupied facility

questions.explanation: 745.227(e)(7)(i)(B): "The soil that is removed shall not be used as top soil at another residential property or child-occupied facility."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: The soil that is removed shall not be used as top soil at another residential property or child-occupied facility.

questions.question: If soil is not removed in a soil abatement, 745.227(e)(7)(ii) requires it to be permanently covered as defined in 745.223. What kind of barrier does that definition describe?

options.A: Solid, relatively impermeable materials, such as pavement or concrete
options.B: A layer of new grass sod
options.C: A thick layer of mulch
options.D: Landscaping materials such as wood chips

questions.explanation: 745.223: permanently covered soil is separated from human contact "by the placement of a barrier consisting of solid, relatively impermeable materials, such as pavement or concrete. Grass, mulch, and other landscaping materials are not considered permanent covering."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.223, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: by the placement of a barrier consisting of solid, relatively impermeable materials, such as pavement or concrete. Grass, mulch, and other landscaping materials are not considered permanent covering.

questions.topic: Inspections, lead hazard screens and risk assessments
questions.question: Under 745.227(c)(1), who may conduct a lead hazard screen?

options.A: A certified renovator
options.B: A person certified by EPA as a risk assessor
options.C: A certified abatement worker
options.D: A certified project designer

questions.explanation: 745.227(c)(1): "A lead hazard screen shall be conducted only by a person certified by EPA as a risk assessor."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Inspections, lead hazard screens and risk assessments
questions.question: How does 745.223 define an inspection?

options.A: A visual check for deteriorated paint, with no report
options.B: Dust wipe testing of floors and window sills after an abatement
options.C: A surface-by-surface investigation to determine the presence of lead-based paint and the provision of a report explaining the results
options.D: Testing of the exterior components of a building only

questions.explanation: 745.223: "Inspection means a surface-by-surface investigation to determine the presence of lead-based paint and the provision of a report explaining the results of the investigation."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.223, Definitions (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: In a risk assessment of a residential dwelling, where does 745.227(d)(5) require dust samples to be collected?

options.A: From the interior window sill(s) and floor in all living areas where one or more children under age 6 are most likely to come into contact with dust
options.B: From window troughs only, in every room of the dwelling
options.C: From the floor of the one room with the most deteriorated paint
options.D: From exterior porches and stoops only

questions.explanation: 745.227(d)(5): "dust samples (either composite or single-surface samples) from the interior window sill(s) and floor shall be collected and analyzed for lead concentration in all living areas where one or more children, under age 6, are most likely to come into contact with dust."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.evidence: dust samples (either composite or single-surface samples) from the interior window sill(s) and floor shall be collected and analyzed for lead concentration in all living areas where one or more children, under age 6, are most likely to come into contact with dust.

questions.question: During which parts of an abatement project does 745.227(e)(2) require the certified supervisor to be onsite?

options.A: Only during post-abatement dust sampling
options.B: Only on the first day of the project
options.C: Only while occupants are present in the building
options.D: During all work site preparation and during the post-abatement cleanup of work areas

questions.explanation: 745.227(e)(2): the certified supervisor "shall be onsite during all work site preparation and during the post-abatement cleanup of work areas." At other times the supervisor must be onsite or available and "able to be present at the work site in no more than 2 hours."

options.D: Within 30 days after the abatement is completed

options.A: The certified inspector who will do the post-abatement testing
options.B: The building owner who contracted for the work

options.D: Any certified abatement worker on the project

questions.question: Under 745.227(e)(8)(i), what must happen if the post-abatement visual inspection finds visible amounts of dust, debris or residue?

options.A: These conditions must be eliminated before the post-abatement testing procedures continue
options.B: Dust samples are taken anyway and the findings are noted in the abatement report
options.C: The job is closed and the findings are given to the owner
options.D: EPA must receive an updated notification before any cleanup

questions.explanation: 745.227(e)(8)(i): "If deteriorated painted surfaces or visible amounts of dust, debris or residue are present, these conditions must be eliminated prior to the continuation of the post-abatement testing procedures."

questions.question: Under 745.227(e)(8)(vii), what is the residual lead level in a composite post-abatement dust sample compared with?

options.A: The action level multiplied by the number of subsamples
options.B: The action level divided by the number of rooms sampled
options.C: The action level unchanged, the same as for a single-surface sample
options.D: The applicable action level divided by half the number of subsamples in the composite sample

questions.explanation: 745.227(e)(8)(vii): a composite sample fails "if the residual lead level in a composite dust sample equals or exceeds the applicable action level divided by half the number of subsamples in the composite sample".

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which condition does 745.227(g) set for composite dust samples?

options.A: They may combine floor and window sill subsamples in one sample
options.B: They shall not consist of subsamples from more than one type of component
options.C: They consist of a single subsample
options.D: They may leave out tested components that look similar to others

questions.explanation: 745.227(g): "Composite dust samples shall consist of at least two subsamples; (2) Every component that is being tested shall be included in the sampling; and (3) Composite dust samples shall not consist of subsamples from more than one type of component."

source.title: eCFR: 40 CFR 745.227, Work practice standards for conducting lead-based paint activities: target housing and child-occupied facilities (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: On or after January 12, 2026, what must the abatement report include when post-abatement dust-lead results are below the dust-lead action levels and at or above the dust-lead reportable levels?

options.A: A new notification to EPA for a second abatement
options.B: A recommendation for a follow-up lead hazard screen
options.C: A dust-lead hazard statement with the language set out in 745.227(e)(10)(vii)
options.D: A statement that the abatement is not complete

questions.explanation: 745.227(e)(10)(vii): "On or after January 12, 2026, when post-abatement dust-lead testing results are below the dust-lead action levels and at or above the dust-lead reportable levels, a dust-lead hazard statement with the following language must be included". The required statement says the project "achieved dust-lead below action levels".
